definition: The raised number $n$ in a power $a^{n}$, also called the index or power; for a positive integer $n$ it counts how many copies of the base $a$ are multiplied together.
$\log_{a} b$ is the exponent you raise the base $a$ to in order to get $b$, so $\log_{a} b = x$ means $a^{x} = b$ (for $a > 0$, $a \neq 1$, $b > 0$).
The logarithm with base $\mathrm{e}$, written $\ln x = \log_{\mathrm{e}} x$; it is the inverse of $\mathrm{e}^{x}$.
